target: bract (PO:0009055) absent (PATO:0000462): the lateral bracts on the fig receptacle are missing, not the fruit
fix: In '<noun> absent', the noun right before 'absent' is the missing part. Never give the absence to the section heading (here fruit).
reason: The text says lateral bracts are absent; the fig is described as present and stipitate.

target: Only the long flagellar branchlets (branch, PO:0025073) have no leaves; the leafy shoots have leaves.
fix: 'leafless <part>' (leafless branchlets, stems, scapes) means that part carries no leaves. Annotate it on that part, never as 'leaf absent' for the whole taxon.
reason: Ficus flagellaris has leaves (their tertiary venation is described). Only the whip-like branchlets are leafless.

target: Basal bracts of the fig (PO:0009055) are not distinct (small or merged), not absent. Make no absence statement.
fix: 'without distinct <part>' and 'not distinct' mean the part is hard to see or blends in. They do not mean it is absent, so make no absence statement.
reason: 'Distinct' hedges the statement; the bracts may still be there. The dark brown strigose text is probably about hairs on another part, but the main error is the absence.

target: trichome (PO:0000282) absent (PATO:0000462): the superficial hairs are missing, not the leaf
fix: '<qualifier> hairs absent' (superficial, stinging, simple, glandular hairs) is the absence of trichome (PO:0000282) on the part being described.
reason: It is the hairs that are absent. 'Cell walls clathrate' describes scale cells, so annotating it as 'leaf reticulate' is also doubtful.

target: No annotation: the bracts were not seen in the specimens examined. Keep only bract deciduous (they are caducous).
fix: 'not seen', 'not known', 'not observed' and 'unknown' mean missing from the material studied. They never mean absent; drop the absence.
reason: Caducous bracts fall early, which is why they were not seen. That does not mean the plant has none.

target: Leaf lamina (PO:0020039) not punctate (PATO:0001512): the dots (pellucid glands) are missing, not the lamina
fix: 'dots absent' and 'without dots' mean the surface is not punctate (no dots or glands). They are a quality of that surface, never the absence of the surface.
reason: The lamina is described (glabrescent beneath); only the dots are missing.

target: No annotation (not seen). Keep bract deciduous.
fix: 'not seen' means not observed, not absent (same rule as X01054).
reason: The bracts are caducous, so they were not seen.

target: lenticel (PO:0000031) absent (PATO:0000462) on the fruit (PO:0009001)
fix: 'without <part>' gives the absence to the named part (here lenticels). The part being described keeps its existence.
reason: The fruit is described as ovoid-ellipsoid; it is the lenticels that are missing.

target: Leaf (PO:0025034) not punctate (PATO:0001512): there are no dots
fix: 'dots absent' means the surface is not punctate (same rule as X01055).
reason: The leaf is described as glossy or dull; only the dots are missing.

target: Location: there are no bracts on the pedicel (PO:0030112), but the bracts below each flower are present and persistent.
fix: In '<part> absent on/at/in <place>', the absence holds only at that place. Annotate the place as lacking the part, never the taxon.
reason: The text gives two different bract positions.

target: No annotation: 'not seen (absent?)' is a doubt, not a statement.
fix: 'not seen', including when a query such as '(absent?)' follows, means not observed. Never record an absence from a question mark.
reason: The author is unsure. The glandular bract probably belongs to the other sex or another inflorescence.

target: No annotation: the male inflorescences and the flowers have not been seen. The female inflorescence is present.
fix: '<parts> not seen' means not observed (same rule as X01054). The sex word ('male inflorescences') also limits the statement to one sex.
reason: The text is about unknown material, and only the male inflorescences; female ones are described.

target: No annotation: the flowers are not seen, not absent.
fix: 'not seen' means not observed (same rule as X01054).
reason: This is a gap in the material. The inflorescence is still described.

target: Fruit (PO:0009001) has no stalk-like base: stalk (PO:0025066, the pseudostalk) absent
fix: 'base without <part>' and '<region> without <part>' mean the named part is absent at that region of the bearer. The bearer itself is present.
reason: It is the pseudostalk that is missing; the fruit and the hairs at its base are present.

target: No absence: the veins (leaf vascular system, PO:0000036) end before the margin. This is how far they reach.
fix: 'not reaching <place>' describes how far a part extends. It is never an absence; make no absence statement.
reason: The veins exist and join near the submarginal vein; they just do not reach the margin.

target: Leaf type: there are no floating leaves, while the submerged leaves are present (with acute apex).
fix: '<kind> leaves absent' (floating, cauline, basal, juvenile leaves) is the absence of that kind of leaf only. Keep the qualifier, or drop the absence when there is no class for that kind.
reason: Potamogeton pectinatus has only submerged leaves.

target: Leaf type: there are no floating leaves, while the submerged leaves are present (with obtuse apex).
fix: Same as X01066: a qualified absence ('floating leaves absent') covers only that kind of leaf.
reason: Potamogeton perfoliatus has only submerged leaves.

target: stipule (PO:0020041) deciduous only. The 'not seen' part gives no absence.
fix: 'caducous, not seen' means the part falls early and so is missing from the specimens. Record deciduous, never absent.
reason: The same sentence produced both annotations; the stipules exist but fall early.

target: Bract (PO:0009055) not glandular: portion of secretory tissue (PO:0005656) absent on the bract
fix: 'glands absent' means the part being described has no glands. It is never the absence of that part.
reason: The probract is described (narrowly elliptic); only the glands are missing.

target: No annotation: the fruit is not known (not observed).
fix: '<part> not known' means not observed (same rule as X01054). If another part of the text describes the part, check whether 'not known' sits under an infraspecific taxon that was merged in.
reason: 'Not known' is about what has been collected, not the plant. The fruit description probably comes from another variety in the same treatment.

target: No annotation: the stipules were not seen.
fix: 'not seen' means not observed (same rule as X01054).
reason: Not observed is not absent. 'Partially fused' probably describes another part (leaflets or sepals) wrongly given to the stipule.

target: corona lobe (FLOPO_0986035) absent: the alternating corona lobes, not the corolla

reason: The corolla is described (ovate lobes); it is the extra alternating corona lobes that are missing.

target: corona lobe (FLOPO_0986035) absent: the alternating lobes of the corona
fix: 'alternating lobes lacking' in a Wrightia corona text gives the absence to the corona lobes. 'Lacking' needs the part that is lacking.
reason: In Wrightia, 'alternating lobes' are corona lobes; the corolla is described as narrow.

target: Different bearers: one part is not lenticellate (for example the fruit or the young twigs) and another is sparsely lenticellate.
fix: 'lenticellate' and 'not lenticellate' are qualities of the part they follow: annotate '<bearer> has_part lenticel (PO:0000031)' or its absence. Never use the lenticel as the bearer.
reason: Both annotations lost their real bearers. In Wrightia, branchlets and fruits differ in lenticels.

target: Part: the climbing stems (PO:0009047) carry no leaves; the few basal leaves are present.
fix: '<part> leafless' and 'leafless <part>' mean that part carries no leaves (same rule as X01051).
reason: Bowiea has a few basal leaves that fall early and leafless twining stems.

target: Stem type: there is no leafy above-ground stem (the plant is acaulescent), but the flowering stem (scape) is present.
fix: 'stemless' and 'acaulescent' mean there is no leafy aerial stem. They do not mean that a flowering stem or scape is absent; never annotate 'stem absent'.
reason: Elytraria acaulis is a rosette herb with bluish green flowering stems.

target: Part: the flowering stem (scape) has no leaves; the leaves of the basal rosette are present (white-felted beneath).
fix: 'with a leafless stem' means the stem carries no leaves (same rule as X01051).
reason: The plant has basal leaves and a leafless flowering stem.

target: Position: there are no sori at the segment apex or in the sinuses; elsewhere along the margin the linear sori are present.
fix: 'absent at/in <region>' limits the absence to that region (same rule as X01059).
reason: Histiopteris has sori along the margin, interrupted at the apex and in the sinuses.

target: trichome (PO:0000282, stinging hair) absent on the plant or stem, not the stipule
fix: 'without stinging hairs' means stinging trichomes are absent (same rule as X01053).
reason: Pilea is the genus of Urticaceae without stinging hairs; the stipules are present and fused.
